candidates.summary: Eval is added to the wide exported ClientAdapter interface for one call site, against this package's own convention of narrow consumer subsets
candidates.failure_scenario: handler_http.go:555 is the only non-test consumer of Eval in the tree, yet the method lands on the exported ClientAdapter, so every implementer has to carry it. The cost is in this diff: MockClient gains a body that can only ever answer "no registry" (client_mock.go:207), so no fixture can drive the registered-user branch, and stubClient gains one that errors by default. The package already has the narrower shape twice and says so in its own words: realm_directory.go:12 declares `pathLister` as "the subset of ClientAdapter the directory depends on", and feature/state/feature.go:17 declares a six-method subset for the same reason. A `userResolver interface { Eval(ctx, pkgPath, expr string) ([]byte, error) }` beside userExists is the house form. ClientAdapter is exported from a library package, so an out-of-tree implementer breaks with no migration note.
candidates.verify_by: grep -rn '\.Eval(' gno.land/pkg/gnoweb --include='*.go' (expect one non-test hit, handler_http.go:555), then read realm_directory.go:9-14 and gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/feature/state/feature.go:15-22 for the precedent; the finding dies if a second consumer exists or if no narrow-subset interface is already in the package
candidates.evidence: grep run at head 876762bd: the only non-test `.Eval(` is `gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/handler_http.go:555: res, err := h.Client.Eval(ctx, "/r/sys/users", ...)`. realm_directory.go:12 `// pathLister is the subset of ClientAdapter the directory depends on.` and feature/state/feature.go:17 `type ClientAdapter interface {` with six methods confirm the convention.
